claim: Common resins absorb at C-H overtone and combination bands near 1,150 to 1,250 nm, 1,370 to 1,420 nm and 1,650 to 1,765 nm, at positions that differ between PET, HDPE, PP, PS and PVC
law: Near-infrared spectroscopy of polymers (Neo et al. 2022, review); open Plastic Scanner prior work
check: Band positions used in WSC-CAL-001 B4; discrete-band identification shown by Plastic Scanner

claim: A standard InGaAs photodiode responds from about 900 to 1,700 nm; the 1,650 nm band is seen with its centroid at 1628 nm and 31 % of its signal at or above 1,650 nm
law: InGaAs band gap cutoff near 1,700 nm at room temperature; responsivity curve of WSC-CAL-001 Table 1
check: Band integral of a Gaussian LED times the responsivity [B1, B2]: centroid 1628 nm

claim: Signal-to-noise ratio on the weakest band in shade (clear item, 8 conversions in 4 cycles) is at least 600, enough to resolve 0.5 % reflectance differences at 3 sigma (fix F2)
law: Shot noise 2qIB and Johnson noise 4kTB/R of the transimpedance stage plus ADC noise

claim: Sunlight through a clear item at 100 klx keeps the 47 kOhm amplifier inside the 2.048 V ADC range
law: Diffuse transmission and view factor of the 36 mm rim; Ohm's law

claim: Ambient error on a clear item backed with the black cap is under 0.5 % of the 1,650 nm signal
law: Interleaved dark subtraction; 10^-3 of the through-light left by the cap
check: 0.208 % <= 0.5 %; rests on the assumed cap leak (10^-3) and ambient change (1 % per 10 ms), to measure at TRL 4
closed_by: WSC-CAL-001 D6 (fix F2); cap opacity at TRL 4

claim: Ambient error on an opaque item is under 0.5 % of the 1,650 nm signal
law: Rim leak of 10^-3 of the clear-item case
check: 0.075 % <= 0.5 %; rests on the assumed rim leak; the black TPU shroud's near-infrared opacity is to confirm
closed_by: WSC-CAL-001 D5; shroud opacity at TRL 4

claim: The dark-level rule refuses an unbacked clear item in sun (dark level above 0.71 times the weakest band)
law: Error budget: 0.5 % limit over the drift of 1 % per 10 ms in a 7 ms gap
check: 936 times the band reading >= 1.241 times the band reading

claim: Button to result in 1.5 s or less
law: Timing budget: 4 cycles of 17 readings of 2 ms settling plus 2 conversions at 330 samples/s, plus classification and display (fix F2)

claim: One 3,000 mAh cell lasts an 8 h shift at 4 scans per minute
law: Energy balance: 80 % of 10.8 Wh over the average draw; an 85 % efficient 3.3 V converter still leaves 18.6 h

claim: A protected 18650 Li-ion cell of 3,000 mAh at 3.6 V stores about 10.8 Wh and is charged at 0 to 45 C only
law: Cell capacity times nominal voltage; IEC 62133-2 (IS 16046 Part 2) cell safety practice
check: 3.0 Ah x 3.6 V = 10.8 Wh; the 45 C charge limit is the usual Li-ion maker limit, to confirm on the chosen cell's datasheet

claim: The 8 MB log partition holds at least 10,000 scans of 64 bytes
law: 8 x 1,048,576 B / 64 B; a margin of 13 times covers file system overhead
check: 131072 scans >= 1e+04 scans

claim: LED light reflected inside the window reaches the detector at under 0.5 % of the signal after the open-air reading, with the window offset changing 10 % between readings (PR-017)
law: Fresnel reflection (4 % per uncoated surface); geometric optics of the baffle through the glass (fix F1); leak through the tube wall
check: 0.0026 % <= 0.5 %; 10 % before fix F1 (Fails, fix proposed); after it the glass path is closed by geometry and the wall leak rests on assumed values (wall opacity 2e-02 or better needed), to confirm on a coupon and a built head at TRL 4

claim: Carbon-black items reflect about 4 % in the near infrared and read 'unknown' below the 0.08 reflectance threshold
law: Carbon black absorbs across the near infrared (WRAP, black plastic packaging)
check: Black item returns 8 % of a typical item; separated with SNR over 257 [C6]; an unbacked clear item (0.10) sits close to the threshold and may read 'unknown', which is the safe side

claim: Corneal irradiance of the brightest LED at 200 mm is inside the IEC 62471 exempt group (100 W/m2)
law: Radiant intensity over distance squared; IEC 62471 exempt limit for infrared radiation to the eye
check: 3.93 W/m2 <= 100 W/m2; limit values as understood from IEC 62471, standard not purchased; 241 W/m2 at the rim if an LED sticks on, so the hardware on-time limit is required
closed_by: WSC-CAL-001 H2; limits to confirm against the standard text

claim: Weighted retinal thermal radiance of the 850 nm LED is under the IEC 62471 exempt limit (weak visual stimulus)
law: Retinal thermal hazard of near-infrared sources, IEC 62471
check: 3.8 % of the limit <= 100 % of the limit; limit values as understood from IEC 62471, standard not purchased
closed_by: WSC-CAL-001 H3; limits to confirm against the standard text

claim: The sun hood gives at least 3:1 display contrast on the part of the screen it shades in 100 klx sun
law: Contrast ratio with diffuse screen reflection of sky light (15 klx)
check: 5.2 :1 >= 3 :1; screen reflectance of 2 % is assumed; a glossy screen reflects sky light specularly (reviewer: about 2:1), so PR-007 stays at risk
closed_by: WSC-CAL-001 I2 to I4; outdoor check at TRL 4

claim: A 1.2 m drop on a shell corner with about 1 mm of crush decelerates the scanner at about 1,200 g
law: Work-energy: deceleration = drop height / stopping distance
check: claimed 1200 g, estimate 1.2e+03 g (ratio 1.00); mean deceleration from an assumed 1 mm crush; the peak of a half-sine pulse is 1.57 times higher (used in S18); crush to measure in the drop test at TRL 4

claim: The printed PETG cell strap stays below the bending strength of printed PETG under the corner-drop cell load
law: Simply supported beam, central peak load: stress = F L / (4 Z); printed PETG about 50 MPa along the layers
check: 34.4 MPa <= 50 MPa; 11 x 10 mm strap at the half-sine peak (fix F3); the 10 x 8 mm strap reached 59 MPa (Fails, fix proposed); rests on the assumed crush (S17), drop test at TRL 4

claim: With LED output falling 0.4 %/C, the 5 % drift warning trips after about 12.5 C of change
law: Linear temperature coefficient (typical for SWIR LEDs; assumed in WSC-CAL-001 Table 1)
check: 0.05 / 0.004 = 12.5 C [J3]; the coefficient is assumed, SWIR LEDs may drift more and shift in wavelength on the steep 1,650 nm detector edge, and a uniform drift cancels in the band ratios while a band-to-band difference does not

claim: PVC in a PET stream spoils the batch because PVC degrades well below PET melt-processing temperatures
law: Thermal dehydrochlorination of PVC releases HCl; PET is melt-processed hot (polymer handbooks)
check: Qualitative claim in WSC-PRB-001; the scanner only reports PVC, it does not depend on the temperatures

claim: Sunlight at about 100 klx carries about 300 W/m2 between 900 and 1,700 nm
law: About 1,000 W/m2 global irradiance at 100 to 120 klx, times the share of a 5,778 K black body between 900 and 1,700 nm (Planck's law, computed here; atmospheric water bands lower it a little)
check: claimed 300 W/m2, estimate 253 W/m2 (ratio 1.19)

claim: The 34 mm body thickness sits in the 32 to 51 mm handle range for a hand grip; the 62 mm width is held like a phone for a light pressing task
law: NIOSH 2004-164 handle diameter for single-handle power tools
check: 34 mm >= 32 mm

claim: Eight discrete bands classify the five resins at 95 % or better on clean, non-black items (PR-001)
law: Paper band study: linear discriminant analysis on log band ratios of approximate reference spectra
check: Not shown at the assumed scatter: 89.5 % at 1.5 % band scatter, 96.7 % at 1.0 %; PE against PP 93 % [B4 to B7]; approximate spectra, train and test from one generator, no 'other' class; needs real item scatter of about 1 % or less; settled only by a labelled item set at TRL 4

claim: Option B: a 2,400 K tungsten filament radiates at least 10 % of its output between 1,550 and 1,850 nm
law: Planck's law, numerical integral

claim: Option B: the MEMS-FPI sensor's 1,550 to 1,850 nm range covers the PE and PP first-overtone bands from 1,680 to 1,765 nm
law: Hamamatsu C13272 series range 1,550 to 1,850 nm (Photonics Online datasheet notice)
check: 1,680 to 1,765 nm lies inside 1,550 to 1,850 nm

claim: Option B: signal-to-noise ratio of at least 200 per 20 nm step on a clear item in shade
law: Lamp irradiance per spectral slice, Lambertian item, shot and Johnson noise

claim: Option B: button to result in about 0.74 s, under 1.5 s
law: Lamp warm-up plus a 100-point filter sweep at an assumed 5 ms per step
check: 0.74 s; the filter settling time per step is to assess from the sensor datasheet

claim: Option B: the five resins can be told apart from 1,550 to 1,850 nm alone
law: First-overtone C-H bands of PE and PP and the aromatic bands of PET and PS lie in this range; PVC's features are weaker
check: Plausible from the band positions of WSC-CAL-001 B4; PVC and PET need a labelled item set

claim: Option B: one 3,000 mAh cell lasts an 8 h shift with the lamps
law: Energy balance with the lamp energy per scan

claim: Option B: the lamps stay clear of softening the black PETG head block (glass transition about 80 C)
law: Average lamp power 0.057 W; bulb glass reaches well above 80 C during each scan
check: Fails, fix proposed at first (bulb 0.2 mm from PETG, independent review); fix F4 in the option B model: each bulb sits in an aluminium sleeve with a 0.2 mm air gap, which spreads the heat to the block; sleeve temperature to confirm
